suggestion_body: Do not exceed one page; condense your impact and eliminate unnecessary text filler.
example_bad: 3-page resume with repetitive text and verbose job duties
example_good: 1 tight page highlighting technical achievements and measurable outcomes

suggestion_body: Avoid 'I' or 'my'; start each bullet point directly with an active verb.
example_bad: I led the engineering team and built my personal payment app
example_good: Led engineering team and built distributed payment platform

suggestion_body: Do not use arbitrary percentage bars; prove skill levels through real-world tech stacks.
example_bad: Python: 85% | React: 90% | Docker: 70%
example_good: Python (FastAPI, PyTest) | React (TypeScript, Redux) | Docker

suggestion_body: Avoid multi-column tables in ATS mode; keep a clean single-column linear reading flow.
example_bad: Tables and parallel sidebars that scramble automated ATS parser extraction
example_good: Clean single-column top-to-bottom layout without embedded tables

suggestion_body: Do not cram dense text into sidebars; reserve narrow columns for skills and contact.
example_bad: Lengthy job experience bullet points crammed inside narrow sidebar
example_good: Contact and core stack on left rail; career history in wide column

suggestion_body: Avoid stray dollar signs; they disrupt automated regex patterns in modern ATS parsers.
example_bad: +1$ optimization in CI/CD deployment pipeline
example_good: Solved N+1 query problem and optimized CI/CD pipeline

suggestion_body: Do not paste broken hyperlinks; use clean, canonical URLs to live repositories and demos.
example_bad: https://github. com/user /temp-draft-repo
example_good: https://github.com/user/ecommerce-platform

suggestion_body: Avoid checkboxes and emojis; use standard round bullets to ensure clean OCR extraction.
example_bad: ☑ Developed payment API with Node.js 🚀
example_good: • Developed resilient microservices payment API with Node.js

suggestion_body: Do not use ambiguous dates; write 'MM/YYYY – Present' or 'MM/YYYY – MM/YYYY' consistently.
example_bad: A couple years ago | 2021 until now | 1.5 years
example_good: 03/2022 – Present

suggestion_body: Avoid vague self-praise adjectives; clearly state your target engineering role and core stack.
example_bad: Passionate developer seeking exciting new tech opportunities
example_good: Full Stack Engineer | React, Node.js, TypeScript

suggestion_body: Do not write your full street address; specify only city and country for privacy.
example_bad: 123 Elm St, Apt 4B, New York, NY 10001
example_good: New York, NY (Open to Remote / Relocation)

suggestion_body: Avoid generic career wishes; summarize key technical strengths and quantified outcomes in three lines.
example_bad: Looking for a dynamic company to expand my technical knowledge
example_good: Backend engineer with 4+ years designing resilient APIs, reducing p99 latency by 30%

suggestion_body: Do not keep random generated numbers; customize a clean LinkedIn URL with your name.
example_bad: https://linkedin.com/in/john-doe-8b29141a
example_good: https://linkedin.com/in/johndoe-dev

suggestion_body: Omit national ID, age, marital status, or photo; international recruiters discard them immediately.
example_bad: National ID: 1234567 | Single | Age: 28 | Photo attached
example_good: Clean professional profile focused solely on engineering credentials and code

suggestion_body: Avoid passive task lists; detail what you achieved, measured by what, doing what (Laszlo Bock).
example_bad: Maintained database servers and investigated slow query alerts
example_good: Cut database query times by 45% through table partitioning and composite indexing

suggestion_body: Avoid passive 'responsible for'; begin each bullet with strong active engineering verbs.
example_bad: Responsible for deploying code and checking backend tasks
example_good: Architected and deployed CI/CD pipelines, decreasing deployment rollbacks by 20%

suggestion_body: Do not state unmeasured claims; support accomplishments with concrete metrics of production impact.
example_bad: Significantly improved application response times and user satisfaction
example_good: Optimized frontend bundles, slashing initial page load time from 3.2s to 1.1s

suggestion_body: Do not write dense paragraphs; keep each achievement bullet to two concise lines.
example_bad: A 6-line paragraph detailing the company administrative backstory and meetings
example_good: Migrated legacy monolith to Go microservices, handling 10k req/s reliably

suggestion_body: Do not put older jobs first; sequence positions in reverse chronological order from present.
example_bad: 2018 junior internship listed as the very first job experience item
example_good: Current senior role (2024 – Present) at the top, followed by earlier positions

suggestion_body: Avoid over-explaining older jobs; give deeper detail and more bullets to recent positions.
example_bad: 5 detailed bullets for a junior support role held 8 years ago
example_good: 4 bullets for your current senior role and 1-2 bullets for past positions

suggestion_body: Do not list disordered tools; group technical skills into clear categories and stacks.
example_bad: JavaScript, Docker, Postgres, React, AWS, Git dumped in a single row
example_good: Frontend: React, TypeScript | Backend: Node.js, Go | DB: PostgreSQL

suggestion_body: Avoid generic soft skills; prove leadership and collaboration through concrete delivered engineering outcomes.
example_bad: Team player, punctual, quick learner, works well under pressure
example_good: Mentored 4 junior engineers and facilitated bi-weekly architecture RFC reviews

suggestion_body: Do not bury core skills; place key technologies near the top for ATS.
example_bad: Technical skills section placed at the very bottom of the second page
example_good: Core technology competencies highlighted within top third of resume

suggestion_body: Do not use lowercase names; use official brand capitalization for accurate ATS matching.
example_bad: typescript, postgresql, docker, reactjs
example_good: TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Docker, React

suggestion_body: Avoid tutorial clone summaries; explain the engineering challenge, architectural decisions, and stack.
example_bad: Built a clone of Netflix by following a YouTube video step by step
example_good: Engineered video streaming platform with serverless AWS Lambda transcoding and CDN

suggestion_body: Never leave projects unverified; include direct links to public source code and live demos.
example_bad: E-commerce platform (runs only locally on my machine at localhost:3000)
example_good: Repo: github.com/user/shop | Live demo: shop-preview.vercel.app

suggestion_body: Do not publish empty repositories; document architecture in a README or include a Dockerfile.
example_bad: Repository with a single 'initial commit' and no setup instructions
example_good: README with system diagram, environment config, and Docker Compose command

suggestion_body: Avoid ambiguous shorthand; state complete official degree title, university name, and graduation year.
example_bad: Tech degree from university (graduated a while ago)
example_good: B.S. in Computer Science | University of Michigan (2019 – 2023)

suggestion_body: Do not include high school if you hold university, tertiary, or technical degrees.
example_bad: High School Diploma | Central High School (2012 – 2016)
example_good: Dedicate document space solely to relevant university and technical education

suggestion_body: Avoid casual short seminar badges; prioritize proctored industry and cloud provider certifications.
example_bad: Attendance certificate for 2-hour online introductory Python workshop
example_good: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (Verifiable Credential ID)

suggestion_body: Do not write arbitrary percentages; use standard international CEFR proficiency levels (B2, C1).
example_bad: English: 75% | French: intermediate level
example_good: English: C1 (Full professional proficiency in engineering environments)
